title: Elevator system design
idea: An elevator design separates two jobs: each car serves its own stops in a sweeping order, and a dispatcher chooses which car answers a hall call.

analogy.text: A shuttle bus on one long street picks up everyone along its way before turning round, instead of driving to stops in the order people waved.
analogy.breaks: Lift riders press buttons at any time, not at fixed stops.

points: A car keeps a set of stops, its floor and its direction.
The LOOK rule: keep going while stops lie ahead, then reverse.
A stop behind the car waits until the car turns, so nobody starves.
A `Dispatcher` scores each car per hall call; the scoring rule is a strategy.

hero.title: One car sweeping up, then down

steps.caption: The car is idle at floor 0. Requests for 5 and 2 arrive (marked floors), so it picks direction up.
Floor 2 lies on the way up, so the car stops there first, before 5.
At floor 3 someone presses 1. It is behind the car, so it waits for the turn.
Floor 5 is served. No stops remain above, so LOOK reverses here.
Going down, the car passes 4, 3 and 2 without stopping. None of them asked.
The car stops at 1. The stop set is empty, so the direction becomes `idle`.

code.title: One car, LOOK order
code.caption: Each `tick()` moves one floor. Change the request on line 28 and predict the new stop order.

walk.text: State is small: floor, direction, and a `Set` of pending stops.
A call at the car's current floor is served at once; others are queued.
The car looks for pending stops above and below its floor.
Keep the current direction while work lies ahead; otherwise turn.
Move one floor, and stop only if that floor is in the set.
A new request arrives mid-trip, as a real rider would press it.

code.title: Choosing a car
code.caption: The dispatcher picks the lowest-cost car per hall call. Replace `cost` with your own rule and compare.

walk.text: An idle car costs only the distance to the caller's floor.
A moving car is cheap only if the call is ahead and wants the same direction.
The dispatcher keeps the cheapest car; on a tie the earlier car wins.
Three hall calls, three winners. At floor 3, A and C tie, so A wins.

pitfalls: Do not serve stops in arrival order; riders on the way get skipped.
Keep scheduling out of the `Elevator` class so the dispatch rule can change alone.
Model direction as a field with clear states, not scattered booleans.

quiz.why: The car heading down serves 2 first. Then it turns and visits the upper stops in ascending order: 7, then 9.

takeaway: Cars sweep their own stops; a dispatcher strategy decides which car answers.

starters: How would I model elevator states with the State pattern?
What changes when I add a second or third car?
How do I handle an emergency stop or overweight alarm?
